scope: Only Casa Mia 94399990 and Villa Marie Antoinette 94401978. Four actual roof components replace the former generic constant-height ordinary frontages.

geometry_source.publisher: IGN BDTopo V3 via Geoplateforme WFS
geometry_source.retained: Literal 3D roof outline coordinates and their separate source ground/maximum-roof metadata. Component 4383 is split along the photographed lower porch chord, with upper duplicated seam corners reconstructed from adjacent main-eave values.

ground_body_source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0, retained buildings.osm.json.gz. Actual mapped ground-body intersection is separate from the larger measured roof envelope.
ground_threshold_source: costa-ground-source.json; 1,632 raw 2 m RGE values with literal response accuracy/measures. Existing 1.5128994113 m relative datum retained. Sample spacing is not accuracy.

primary_visual_sources.publisher: Les Ballets de Monte-Carlo, property operator
primary_visual_sources.copyright: ©AB, Les Ballets de Monte-Carlo. Review only, no game texture reuse.
primary_visual_sources.observed: Pink plaster villa, rough pale-stone lower gallery, paired arched upper openings, deep three-arch porch with cylindrical columns/lattice balustrade, deep dark eaves and terracotta roof.

primary_visual_sources.rights: Review only. No image pixels or textures are shipped. Open IGN/OSM data supplies source geometry.
primary_visual_sources.observed: Separate hipped main roof with an inset gray cap, a low porch, a west wing and an elongated east wing. Terraced planting and stairs occupy the garden in front of the villa.

primary_visual_sources.publisher: Direction de la Prospective, de l’Urbanisme et de la Mobilité, Gouvernement Princier
primary_visual_sources.title: PU-C3-MCO-Z1-D4, landscape and heritage plan,1:500,2021-02-25
primary_visual_sources.observed: Casa Mia core and separate lower wing, stairs and garden J1. This regulatory plan indicates parcel context; proposed garden/height rules are not treated as a completed construction survey.
Construction within Casa Mia garden is conditional on restoring its landscape and equivalent tree count. No above-ground building is invented from the proposed underground dance-hall volume.

Continuous T1 approach shows the low Casa west wing in salmon stucco, with small dark arched openings and a pale cornice above the separate Larvotto arch. This qualifies the west-wing material/opening treatment, not a changed roof/body envelope. Neighboring ornate apartments overlap east/Antoinette in perspective; their details are not indiscriminately transferred.

reconstruction_estimates.roof_hips: Insets 4.2/1.5/3.4/2.5 m for core/west/east/Antoinette are metric architectural estimates within actual source outlines. Hipped tile bands and gray core cap follow primary imagery; exact internal ridges are unmeasured. Source peak fields bound the reconstructed caps.
reconstruction_estimates.visible_storeys: Casa core has three photographed upper rows,3.6 m reconstructed floor pitch with 40.5 m absolute lower porch deck. Other components use three conservative 3.2/3.4 m upper rows within measured roofs; exact basement/storey layouts remain unmeasured. No global minimum-terrain roof placement is used.
reconstruction_estimates.porch: Three actual photographed open upper/lower arches; 4 m gallery depth/height, columns 0.22 m radius, arch rise 0.8/0.85 m and lattice divisions 0.3 m are explicit metric estimates. Deck/support footprints stay within the actual mapped property.
reconstruction_estimates.materials: Existing original pink plaster, limestone, terracotta, timber and neutral glass materials. Review photographs are never used as texture assets.
reconstruction_estimates.west_wing_facade: Salmon stucco reuses MonacoRuscinoRose. Single small arched openings retain the existing three upper rows and existing bay positions/pale cornices. Geometry of all four measured roofs, their support/body intersections and the unchanged ground datum remains fixed.

preservation: Native racing road, survey/control profiles, terrain.bin, vehicle tuning and camera unchanged. Existing terrain is not flattened or recolored to hide the hill. Source-qualified land-cover work is a separate follow-up.
remaining_limits: Rose de France has conflicting partial source heights and is unchanged.
The 2019 orthophoto and owner photograph do not establish the supplied edited clip’s precise season; the terrace/roof interpretation is bounded accordingly.
The source geometry does not survey openings, balustrades, hip ridges, materials or basement floor elevations.
The inner west-roof aerial detail may be a lightwell/skylight; no unsupported courtyard hole is cut from the literal IGN component.
